My mind feels like sludge, and focusing on schematics or designs is nearly impossible. I end up just staring at my screen, feeling drained after just a few minutes of trying to concentrate. I’ve been crying a lot, too, often for no real reason, just sudden bursts of tears I can’t hold back. And honestly, sometimes I just think, "I wish I wasn't here," or "I just want it to end." I don't have a plan, but the thoughts are there.

Then, about a month ago, things shifted. I suddenly had this surge of energy. I was working on four different projects at once, pulling all-nighters and feeling completely fine, like sleep wasn't even necessary. My thoughts were racing, and I couldn't stop talking – just felt this need to fill every silence. There were times I’d be pacing my apartment, wringing my hands, just this restless energy I couldn’t burn off. My mood was all over the place too; one minute I’d feel on top of the world, and the next I’d snap at someone for the smallest thing. It was intense, and honestly, a bit jarring, especially after feeling so low for so long. It was after... that incident years ago, things never quite went back to normal, but these ups and downs feel different.
D009-D018_h001.question_a:
I'm a 30-year-old automotive engineer, and lately, things have been… a lot. For about a month now, I’ve been feeling this surge of energy. I barely sleep – maybe an hour or two a night – but I don’t even feel tired. In fact, I'm getting so much done at work, starting multiple projects, and I can't seem to stop talking. My thoughts race, and I get really agitated, pacing around my apartment because I just can't sit still for a moment. My mood's all over the place, too; one minute I'm ecstatic, the next I snap at someone.

But for the past year, it's been the complete opposite. I just feel utterly drained. I've been crying a lot, and I haven't had the motivation to do anything, either at work or in my personal life. Even thinking feels like a monumental effort. Sometimes, I just think, "I want to die," or "I wish I could just disappear," though I’d never actually do anything. It's really affecting my work and my life outside of it. I know I went through a really rough car accident a few years ago, but these ups and downs, particularly the irritability and not being able to sleep, seem to come and go on their own, completely separate from thinking about the accident.
D009-D018_h001.question_b:
"Lately, I just can't seem to catch a break. For the past year, I've felt this heavy cloud over me. Honestly, a lot of days, I just wish I wouldn’t wake up – I think about dying, though I haven't made any plans.

Then, about a month ago, things shifted dramatically. I was suddenly full of energy, working late into the night on multiple projects, jumping from one idea to the next. Sleep? Didn't need it. My words just tumble out, I can’t seem to stop talking, and I pace endlessly in my office, too restless to sit still. This burst of energy and activity, it feels different though. It's been… a very strange year, doctor. I’m not really myself. For the past month or so, I’ve felt this incredible burst of energy, like I could conquer anything. My husband, bless his heart, says I’m running on fumes, but I don’t feel tired at all. I can get by on just a couple of hours of sleep and still be up at dawn, ready to tackle a dozen showings. I find myself talking a mile a minute, jumping from one idea to the next about new listings or marketing strategies. Sometimes, I just can’t sit still; I’ll pace around the office or wring my hands without even realizing I’m doing it. It feels productive, but also a bit much.

But then, before this most recent burst, for about a year, it was the complete opposite. I just felt… heavy. Everything was a monumental effort. Getting out of bed felt like lifting lead. The joy of closing a sale, or even just a beautiful sunset, completely vanished. It was like living under a grey cloud. And sometimes, these really unsettling thoughts would flash through my mind – like a sudden urge to just step off the curb into traffic. I mean, I never would, but the thought just pops in, unbidden. It made it really hard to focus on work; my sales have definitely suffered. I just feel so disconnected from everything, like there’s a distance between me and the world. Sometimes, memories of what happened… they just replay in my mind, making it hard to concentrate. I try to push them away.

It’s hard to pinpoint exactly when things started feeling off, but for the past nine months or so, I’ve been shrouded in this pervasive gloom. It’s more than just feeling down; it's a persistent, heavy blanket that smothers everything. Even after a full night’s rest, I wake up utterly drained, like I haven't slept a wink. And getting a full night's rest is a luxury – I often wake up in the middle of the night, my mind racing, and then struggle to drift back to sleep. This fatigue makes lecturing an immense challenge; my usual sharp intellect feels dulled.

Then there are these other periods, much shorter, like the three weeks I experienced a couple of months ago. It was… exhilarating, in a way. I felt like I could conquer anything, buzzing with an energy I hadn't felt in years. I started outlining two new books, completely convinced I’d finish them before the semester ended. My wife also mentioned my increased interest in intimacy during that time. But it also came with a lot of anger, I found myself snapping at students and colleagues over minor things, quickly flipping from feeling on top of the world to intensely irritable. It didn't affect my work too much, if anything I was *more* productive, but my wife certainly noticed the rapid shifts. I've also had this recurring, unsettling image flash in my mind, almost like a scene I've witnessed, though I can't quite place it. It's fleeting, but disturbing.
D009-D018_h012.question_a:
"Lately, I'm just… all over the place. For about three weeks last month, I felt like I was firing on all cylinders – sleeping only a few hours but buzzing with ideas, convinced I could write a whole new textbook, start a research project, and even revamp the department curriculum all at once. I felt utterly brilliant, like the most capable person on campus, and my wife even commented on how… hands-on I was being with her. My mood was jumping around, though; one minute I was ecstatic, the next I'd snap at someone for a minor interruption. It was intense, but I was still getting everything done, even if I was a bit much for everyone.

But then, for the past nine months now, it’s been the complete opposite. I just feel profoundly sad, heavy, like I'm dragging myself through mud. Getting out of bed is a Herculean task, and I'm exhausted no matter how much I rest. I wake up constantly in the middle of the night, my mind racing. It’s hard to focus on my lectures, and I’ve missed quite a few deadlines, which is completely unlike me. I did go through a pretty rough car accident a couple of years ago, and I suppose that was traumatic, but these mood shifts and sleep issues, they pop up out of nowhere, long after the accident, and they don't seem connected to it at all. It's not like the accident is constantly replaying or anything; this just happens in waves."

I’m constantly exhausted, even after sleeping for what feels like a decent amount of time. And speaking of sleep, I keep waking up in the middle of the night, sometimes several times, and then I just lie there, mind racing. It’s definitely affecting my work; I’m losing my focus, and it’s harder to prepare for my lectures.

Before all this truly hit, about a year ago, actually around the time of that terrible accident on campus, I had a strange period lasting about three weeks. I was on top of the world, felt like I could accomplish anything – even started three new research projects at once! My wife actually commented on my boundless energy and how much... 'affectionate' I was being. But that passed.

The current issues, though, the fatigue and the broken sleep, they really took hold after the accident. It’s like my body hasn’t been able to settle since then, constantly on edge. It’s not like these sleep issues or this constant irritability come and go; they’ve been pretty much steady since that day, a stark change from before."

I don’t care about the shop anymore, even though I built it up myself, brick by brick after Ellen passed. I find myself pacing, picking at my cuticles until they bleed, just can’t sit still even though I’m so worn out.

My lads at the shop, they look at me like I’ve grown a second head. I’ve been working non-stop, really. Staying up for days, prepping orders, drawing up new specials at 3 AM. I don’t feel tired at all, just buzz with energy. I’ve probably gotten more done in the last few weeks than in the last year, but it's not normal for me. I pace a lot, can’t sit still, picking at my cuticles without even realizing it. Even when the shop is busy and I’m making good money, it just feels… empty. I don’t feel joy or sadness, just this hollow feeling. It's like my accomplishments don't even register. I remember a horrific car crash I witnessed right after work one night. Ever since then, it feels like this constant hyper-alertness, this jumpiness, and the trouble sleeping, they just never really go away. They're not like those other times that come and go; it’s all connected to what I saw.
